correctness.rationale: Every edge creates an equitable 2m-cell distance partition by uniqueness of paths shorter than m; its Laplacian quotient is a single edge parallel to a 2m−1-bundle series chain with explicitly counted conductances. The potential is cell-constant because the dipole source belongs to the invariant subspace; direct exact current sums yield the two induced operator norms for every edge without assuming flag-transitivity. The equal-order sign change follows from exact evaluations R_m(2,2)>1>R_m(3,3) and monotonicity. Eight grounded-Laplacian cases independently check 312 full columns and eight diameter/girth pairs, with 70 exact equal-order formula tests. The finite cases only corroborate the general proof.

originality.rationale: The complete exact canonical edge cut/cycle endpoint norms and order-two/order-three sign reversal have not been identified in inspected projection, finite-geometry and flag-association-scheme primary literature. The 2023 projection study computes the Hamming cube and develops general tools; the 2006 regular-partition paper treats combinatorial quotients but not absolute electrical-current column norms; the 2024 flag scheme treats a different operator algebra. Public indexed results on generalized quadrangles concern Rips persistence and other invariants, not these projections. This is a supported literature comparison, not an exhaustive novelty certificate.

value.rationale: A natural complete class of finite thick high-girth incidence geometries receives exact graph-independent Banach cut/cycle endpoint projection norms, including non-flag-transitive examples. The edge-rooted quotient is a structural reduction across all four feasible thick polygon diameters, while equal-order cases exhibit a universal discrete reversal between q=2 and q≥3 of the maximizing projection norm. The precise invariants motivate potential comparison of inequivalent incidence geometries and extension to distance-biregular graphs; no downstream theorem is claimed.
